title: Headache
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with chronic daily headache (worse in morning, with Valsalva), transient visual obscurations, pulsatile tinnitus, and diplopia (CN VI palsy from increased ICP). Fundoscopy: bilateral papilledema. IIH is elevated ICP without mass lesion or hydrocephalus, typically in obese women of childbearing age. Risk factors: obesity, recent weight gain, vitamin A excess, tetracyclines, OCPs, steroids. Diagnosis: MRI/MRV brain (normal — rules out mass, venous sinus thrombosis). LP: elevated opening pressure (>25 cm H2O) with normal CSF composition. Treatment: weight loss (most important), acetazolamide (carbonic anhydrase inhibitor — reduces CSF production). Serial ophthalmology: visual fields, optic nerve exam. If vision threatened: optic nerve sheath fenestration or CSF shunting (VP or LP shunt). Discontinue causative medications.
chief_complaint: Chronic headache, transient visual loss, pulsatile tinnitus
